However, some accounts claim that during the Dutch colonial era in Indonesia, around the reign of King Rama I, dessert-making methods from Indonesia had an impact on its growth.

Because of its layered look, which is sometimes connected to prosperity and advancement, Khanom Chan has become a well-known traditional delicacy in Thailand and is frequently made for important celebrations and auspicious events.
Banh Da Lon (Vietnamese: bánh da lợn, lit. ‘pig skin cake’) is a traditional Vietnamese steamed layered dessert that is especially popular in southern Vietnam.
The dessert is also commonly prepared for other important occasions, including the Mid-Autumn Festival (Tết Trung Thu), the Ullambana Festival (Vu Lan), and various family gatherings.
Its popularity is attributed not only to its sweet flavor but also to its symbolic layered structure, which is often interpreted as representing good fortune, prosperity, and continuity.

name: Khanom chin
summary: Khanom chin or khanom jeen are fresh, thin white rice noodles in Thai cuisine which are made from rice fermented for three days, boiled, and extruded through into boiling water through a sieve.
story_candidates: Although chin means "Chinese" in Thai, this type of noodle originated from the Mon people.

name: Khanom farang kudi chin
summary: Khanom farang kudi chin (Thai: ขนมฝรั่งกุฎีจีน, pronounced [kʰā.nǒm fā.ràŋ kū.dīː tɕīːn]) is a Thai-style cake that was influenced by Portuguese desserts since the Ayutthaya era, during the reign of King Narai (1633–88).
fun_fact_candidates: After the fall of Ayutthaya and during the reign of King Taksin (1767–82), people migrated from the former capital to the new one located on Chao Phraya's west bank (now Thonburi), which included a number of Portuguese people.
They were permitted to settle there by the king and intermarry with the Thais.
To this day, they have inherited legacies from their ancestors, such as Christianity and some western traditions.
It is topped with raisins, dried sweet gourds, and white sugar, which are symbols of good luck, and is made without using any baking powder or yeast.

learn_more.title: Books about Khanom farang kudi chin (Open Library)

name: Khanom kho
summary: Khanom tom (Thai: ขนมต้ม, pronounced [kʰā.nǒm tôm]) and khanom kho (ขนมโค, [kʰā.nǒm kʰōː]) are closely related traditional Thai desserts.
fun_fact_candidates: They are served at ceremonies, festivals, parties, and weddings.

name: Khanom tan
summary: Khanom tan (Thai: ขนมตาล; pronounced [kʰā.nǒm tāːn]) is a traditional Thai dessert consisting of small steamed cakes flavoured with toddy palm sugar and coconut milk, wrapped in banana leaves, and topped with grated coconut.
story_candidates: The Thai term tan /taːn˧/ (Thai: ตาล) has its origins in the Indic language, as evidenced by its appearance in the Ram Khamhaeng Inscription No. 1 Face 3 Line 13, dated to 1292 CE.

During that time, the main ingredients used in preparing desserts were rice flour, sugar and coconut, in contrast to desserts from the later Ayutthaya period, which are based on a mixture of eggs and sugar.
Today, Khanom Tan is not well known among younger generations due to its disappearance from street markets, but it is still a popular Thai dessert outside of the Bangkok area.

name: Khanom thuai
summary: Khanom thuai talai (Thai: ขนมถ้วยตะไล, Thai pronunciation: [kʰā.nǒm tʰûaj tā.lāj]), usually shortened to khanom thuai (ขนมถ้วย), is a Thai dessert made from rice flour, coconut milk and sugar.
story_candidates: In the past, Khanom Thuai was generally made only for important cultural dates and festivals, such as weddings, ordinations, and events similar to Songkran day.

name: Khao kha mu
summary: Khao kha mu or khao kha moo (Thai: ข้าวขาหมู, pronounced [kʰâːw kʰǎː mǔː], lit. 'rice leg-pork'; Chinese: 猪脚饭, pinyin: zhū jiǎo fàn), or sometimes simply called kha mu (ขาหมู), is a popular Thai food.
fun_fact_candidates: For Bangkok, there are many famous khao kha mu restaurants in various neighbourhoods such as Bang Wa, Phlapphla Chai, Mo Mi, Sam Yan, etc.
A restaurant in Bang Rak received Bib Gourmand awards in both 2018 and 2019 Michelin Guide.

learn_more.title: Books about Khao kha mu (Open Library)

name: Khao khluk kapi
summary: Khao khluk kapi (Thai: ข้าวคลุกกะปิ, pronounced [kʰâːw kʰlúk kāpìʔ]; sometimes spelled as khao kluk kapi) is a flavorful dish in Thai cuisine that consists of the primary ingredients of fried rice mixed with shrimp paste, the latter of which is known as "kapi" in Thai.
story_candidates: Khao khluk kapi's recipe was adapted from an original Mon dish during the time of King Rama II.
It is originated in Central Thailand (historical Mon settlement region), and is typically served as a lunch dish in Thailand.

learn_more.title: Books about Khao khluk kapi (Open Library)

name: Khao soi
summary: Khao soi or khao soy (Thai: ข้าวซอย, pronounced [kʰâ(ː)w sɔ̄ːj]; Lanna: ᩮᨡᩢ᩶ᩣᨪᩬ᩠ᨿ, pronounced [kʰa᷇(ː)w sɔ̄ːj]; Lao: ເຂົ້າຊອຍ, pronounced [kʰȁ(ː)w sɔ́ːj]; Shan: ၶဝ်ႈသွႆး, pronounced [kʰaw˧˧˨.sʰɔj˥]; Burmese: အုန်းနို့ခေါက်ဆွဲ, pronounced [ʔóʊɴ no̰ kʰaʊʔ sʰwɛ́]) is a dish served in Northern Thailand.
fun_fact_candidates: The dish is believed to have evolved from Chin Haw Muslim traders who plied the spice route when what is now modern-day northern Thailand was controlled by the Burmese.
Traditionally, the dough for the wheat noodles is spread out on a cloth stretched over boiling water.

name: Khao tom
summary: Khao tom (Lao: ເຂົ້າຕົ້ມ, pronounced [kʰȁ(ː)w.tôm]) and khao tom mat (Thai: ข้าวต้มมัด, pronounced [kʰâ(ː)w.tôm mát]) are a popular Laotian and Thai dessert made of sticky rice, ripe banana, coconut milk, all wrapped and steamed-cooked in banana leaves.
fun_fact_candidates: A similar dessert is enjoyed throughout Southeast Asian countries where it is known as num ansom in Khmer, lepet in Indonesian, suman in Filipino, and bánh tét and bánh chưng in Vietnamese.
story_candidates: In Laos, sticky rice is a national staple food and steeped in the Lao culture and religious traditions.
Khao tom is offered during the Lao baci ceremony held to commemorate special occasions, such as starting a new job, marriage, housewarming, birth of a new baby, and celebration of Lao New Year.
Furthermore, khao tom is a popular snack sold during festivals, in markets and food stalls around the country.
It was listed in a collection of recipes for favorite dishes of the former Lao royal family written by Phia Sing (1898-1967), the king's personal chef and master of ceremonies.

In Thailand, the Sai Krachat tradition (ประเพณีใส่กระจาด), also known as Suea Krachat or Soe Krachat in Phuan language, is a merit-making Buddhist tradition of the Thai Phuan people of Ban Mi District, Lopburi Province.
It takes place on the eve of the Great Birth Sermon celebration.
In Thailand, khao tom mat is the symbol of couples because for boiling usually the leaf wraps are bundled to sets of two.
Khao tom mat is also a traditional Thai dessert for Ok Phansa Day (the end of Buddhist lent in late October.), but it is then called khao tom luk yon (Thai: ข้าวต้มลูกโยน).

In 2014, the Department of Cultural Promotion under the Ministry of Culture registered khao tom mat as an intangible cultural heritage, in the Knowledge and Practices Concerning Nature and the Universe category, to prevent them from being lost along with other cultural heritage.

name: Kluai buat chi
summary: Kluai buat chi or banana in coconut milk (Thai: กล้วยบวชชี, pronounced [klûa̯j bùa̯t t͡ɕʰīː]) is a Thai dessert.
fun_fact_candidates: The dessert is widely served throughout Thailand and is popular in neighboring countries such as Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, and Malaysia.

learn_more.title: Books about Kluai buat chi (Open Library)

name: Koi (dish)
summary: Koi (Lao: ກ້ອຍ; Thai: ก้อย, Thai pronunciation: [kɔ̂j]) is a "salad" dish of the Lao people living in modern-day Laos Isan, Thailand and Thai people of Vietnam (Son La province) consisting of raw meat denatured by acidity, usually from lime juice.
fun_fact_candidates: Koi made with raw fish is a popular dish in Laos and Isaan and a common source of infection with the Southeast Asian liver fluke Opisthorchis viverrini.
It is believed to be a cause of cholangiocarcinoma via liver fluke transmission.

name: Krating Daeng
summary: Krating Daeng (Thai: กระทิงแดง, RTGS: krathing daeng, pronounced [krà.tʰīŋ dɛ̄ːŋ]; lit. 'red bull' or 'red gaur') is a Thai non-carbonated energy drink brand created by Chaleo Yoovidhya.
story_candidates: Krating Daeng was first devised in 1975.
Krating Daeng has lost its leadership position in its home market of Thailand to M-150 and is now third in the country's energy drinks market, down to possibly only 7 percent market share in 2014.

name: Kung sarong
summary: Kung sarong (Thai: กุ้งโสร่ง, pronounced [kûŋ sā.ròŋ]) is a Thai dish which contains deep fried prawns wrapped in egg noodles.

name: La tiang
summary: La tiang (Thai: ล่าเตียง, pronounced [lâː tīaŋ]) is an ancient Thai snack.
fun_fact_candidates: It is most well known from the Kap He Chom Khrueang Khao Wan poem composed during the reign of King Rama I by the crown prince who later became King Rama II.

name: Lao khao
summary: Lao khao (Thai: เหล้าขาว, pronounced [lâw kʰǎːw]; lit. 'white spirit') or officially sura khao (Thai: สุราขาว, [sùʔ.rāː kʰǎːw]) is a Thai distilled spirit.
story_candidates: According to the Chinese source “Yingya Shenglan” (1405–1433), the Ayutthaya Kingdom, called Xiānluó (暹羅) by the Chinese, had two kinds of spirits, both of which are distilled spirits.

Of Rice they do at first make Beer, which they drink not; but they convert it into Aqua Vitae which they call Laou, and the Portuguese Arak, an Arabian word, which properly signifies sweat, and metaphorically essence, and by way of excellence Aqua Vitae.
Of the Rice Beer they likewise make Vinegar.” In 1790, during the reign of King Rama I, Bangyikhan Liquor Distillery was known to have been established.
In 1834, English sources mention that exports of Siam included white spirits distilled from glutinous rice.
Distilling lao khao in Thailand must be licensed, under the Criminal Activities Act which was introduced in the 1950s.
The metals were switched out with stainless steel when the government took over all distilleries by 1960.
By 1984, only twelve distilleries were left.
ThaiBev then took control of these twelve distilleries in 1985, forming a monopoly.
In 2003, Thaksin Shinawatra fulfilled an election promise made during the 2001 Thai general election to let people produce the spirits with licenses, thus breaking the monopoly.

name: Larb
summary: Laab / Larb (Lao: ລາບ; Thai: ลาบ, RTGS: lap, pronounced [lâːp], also spelled laap, larp, or lahb) is a type of Lao meat salad that is the national dish of Laos, along with green papaya salad and sticky rice.
story_candidates: Another French visitor, Doctor Estrade, who arrived in 1893, described laab as a Lao main dish made with boiled fish, chili and ground roasted sticky rice.
Laab can be served raw, which is known as laab diip (raw) or aharn suer (tiger food), or cooked, and usually served with a soup made with the bones of the meat being used.

Historically, laab dishes were more common amongst the aristocracy and traditional recipes for laab served to Laotian royalty are in a collection of handwritten recipes from Phia Sing (1898–1967), royal chef and master of ceremonies.

Laab is considered to be an auspicious and lucky dish because traditionally meat was not readily available, and most Laotians would normally eat laab at special occasions, such as wedding, New Year celebrations and festivals.
During the New Year celebration, many Lao families believe that eating laab on day one of the three-day celebration will bring good fortune for the rest of the year.

As tradition goes, the head of the family would start with malaxating the mincemeat – softening and incorporating it with a cupful of stock from the soup, then adding the toasted ground rice, pepper powder, garlic, salt, padaek sauce and finally chopped aromatics before serving.
Laab has a meaning in the Lan Na dialect (1292–1775), the neighboring kingdom of Lan Xang (1353–1707, present day Laos).
In 2026, Laos submitted an application to UNESCO seeking to declare laab as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

name: Mamuang kuan
summary: Mamuang kuan (Thai: มะม่วงกวน, Thai pronunciation: [mā.mûaŋ kūan]), also referred to as preserved mango or mango leather, is a traditional Thai sweet.
fun_fact_candidates: Traditionally, the mango is then sun-dried for multiple days, but this may be accelerated with a conventional oven.

name: Mango sticky rice
summary: Mango sticky rice is a traditional Southeast Asian and South Asian dessert made with glutinous rice, fresh mango and coconut milk.

learn_more.title: Books about Mango sticky rice (Open Library)

name: Massaman curry
summary: Massaman curry (Thai: แกงมัสมั่น, RTGS: kaeng matsaman, pronounced [kɛ̄ːŋ mát.sā.màn] ) is a Thai dish consisting of potatoes, onions, peanuts, and massaman curry paste cooked in coconut milk, generally with chicken added.
fun_fact_candidates: The substance of the dish is usually based on chicken, potatoes, onions, and peanuts.
story_candidates: Hence, many earlier writers from the mid-19th century called the dish "Mussulman curry".

According to Thai journalist and scholar Santi Sawetwimon, as well as Thai food experts David Thompson and Hanuman Aspler the dish originated in 17th century central Thailand at the cosmopolitan court of Ayutthaya, through the Persian merchant Sheik Ahmad Qomi, from whom the noble Thai Bunnag family descends.
The curry is extolled in the poem Kap He Chom Khrueang Khao Wan from the end of the 18th century, attributed to Prince Itsarasunthon of Siam (now Thailand), the later King Rama II (1767–1824).
It is dedicated to a lady who is thought to be Princess Bunrot, the later Queen Sri Suriyendra, wife of King Rama II.

The second stanza of the poem reads: The first-ever recorded recipe for massaman curry by Lady Plean Phatsakorawong in 1889: "Chicken Massaman curry with bitter orange juice", with Massaman spelled Matsaman (หมัดสมั่น).
By 2002, it was being included in Australian recipe books as "Musaman beef curry".
In 2011, CNNGo ranked massaman curry as the number one most delicious food in an article titled "World's 50 most delicious foods".
It remained at number one in the official, updated 2018 version.

name: Mekhong (spirit)
summary: Mekhong (แม่โขง) is Thailand's first domestically produced branded golden spirit.
fun_fact_candidates: It is also known as "The Spirit of Thailand".
story_candidates: In 1914, the ownership of the privately owned Sura Bangyikhan Distillery (lit.
The concession agreement expired in 1927 during the reign of King Prajadhipok.
The Department then cancelled the concession for spirit distillation and distribution before taking over the spirit production on 1 April 1929.
Later, the Excise Department concocted another blended spirit using herbs combined with a traditional medicated liquor recipe.
The Kham Khong song was very popular and avidly instilled a patriotic sense into the hearts of Thai people.
Such a dramatic effect influenced the Excise Department to use "Mekhong" to name the 35-degree special blended spirit that was newly produced in 1941.

Mekhong Rum is mentioned several times on the album Hell's Ditch by The Pogues, along with other common Thai drinks. "Mekhong" (Mekong) is also the name of a popular song recorded by The Refreshments on the album Fizzy Fuzzy Big & Buzzy.

name: Mi krop
summary: Mi krop (Thai: หมี่กรอบ, pronounced [mìː krɔ̀ːp]), also spelled mee krob, is a Thai dish consisting of deep-fried rice vermicelli noodles with a sweet and sour sauce.
story_candidates: A legend claims that King Rama V visited the people by boat in the Talad Phlu area and smelled the noodles that a Chinese immigrant named "Chin Li" (จีนหลี) was stir-frying at that time.
In Bangkok, there are at least two restaurants famous for Mi krop.

One is Chin Li Restaurant, also known as Tek Heng, in Talad Phlu on the Thon Buri side, directly connected to the original legend of Chin Li's noodles, and the other is Mit Ko Yuan in Phra Nakhon, near the Giant Swing and Bangkok City Hall.

name: Miang kham
summary: Miang kham (Thai: เมี่ยงคำ, pronounced [mîaŋ kʰām]; Lao: ໝ້ຽງຄຳ, pronounced [mȉaŋ kʰám]; pronounced [mìaŋ kʰâm]; Lanna: ᨾ᩠᩶ᨿᨦᨤᩴᩣ, pronounced [mi᷇aŋ kʰām]) is a traditional Southeast Asian snack from Thailand and Laos.
fun_fact_candidates: It was introduced to the Siamese court of King Rama V by Princess Dara Rasmi.
story_candidates: Miang kham is a snack food that originated in the Lao regions of Thailand, originally using pickled tea leaves (called miang in the northern Thai language).
The dish is mentioned in Epic of the Verse of Foods, a book written by King Rama II.
It is also popular in the Central Region of Thailand.

name: Mu kratha
summary: Mu kratha (Thai: หมูกระทะ, RTGS: mu kratha, pronounced [mǔː krā.tʰáʔ]) is a Southeast Asia cooking method, originating in Thailand.
fun_fact_candidates: In the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia, and Myanmar it is known as mookata.
In Laos, it is known as sin dat (Lao: ຊີ້ນດາດ).
story_candidates: Mu kratha became popular in Thailand during the late 20th century, especially in the 19s, as buffet-style dining gained popularity.

name: Naem (food)
summary: Naem is a pork sausage in Lao and Thai cuisine.
fun_fact_candidates: It is a popular Southeast Asian food, and different regions of Southeast Asia have various preferred flavors, including variations of sour and spicy.

name: Nam chim
sections: Shared dishes > Dipping sauces and pastes
summary: Nam chim or nam jim (Thai: น้ำจิ้ม, IPA: [ná(ː)m tɕîm]) is Thai for "dipping sauce".
fun_fact_candidates: Although Sriracha sauce is commonly known as sot Sriracha in Thailand (sot is the Thai pronunciation of the English word sauce), it is sometimes called nam chim Sriracha or nam phrik Sriracha.
Many of the ingredients in a nam chim are finely chopped or pounded in a mortar and pestle or, non-traditionally, ground in a blender.
story_candidates: Many types of nam chim used in different dishes are mentioned in various cookbooks, including Mae Khrua Hua Pa (1908–1909) by Lady Plean Phatsakorawong, and "Nang Suea Kap Khao Son Luklan Kap Pholmai Khong Wang Lae Khanom" (1876-1961) by Mrs. Kleep Mahitorn.

name: Nam khao
summary: Naem khao (Lao: ແໜມເຂົ້າ), also known as yam naem (Thai: ยำแหนม) is a very popular Lao appetizer salad originating from Tha Deua, a small port village, in Vientiane, Laos.
fun_fact_candidates: Nam khao can be found at street stalls, restaurants, or served communal/potluck style on large trays at parties and other celebratory events.
The dish is also gaining popularity in the West where Laotians have immigrated.
It was also named among the best street foods in Asia.

name: Nam ngiao
summary: Nam ngiao (Thai: น้ำเงี้ยว, pronounced [ná(ː)m ŋía̯w]) or nam ngio (Thai: น้ำงิ้ว, pronounced [ná(ː)m ŋíw]) is a noodle soup or curry of the cuisine of the Tai Yai people who live in the northeast of Myanmar, the southwest of Yunnan province, China, and in northern Thailand, mainly in Mae Hong Son Province.
fun_fact_candidates: The dish has become famous in the northern Thai cuisine.

name: Nam phrik
sections: Shared dishes > Dipping sauces and pastes
summary: Nam phrik (Thai: น้ำพริก, pronounced [ná(ː)m pʰrík̚]) is a type of Thai spicy chili sauce typical of Thai cuisine.
fun_fact_candidates: In the traditional way of preparing these sauces, the ingredients are pounded together using a mortar and pestle, with either salt or fish sauce added to taste.
story_candidates: The first Westerner to report of nam phrik was Simon de la Loubère, a French ambassador to the court of Ayutthaya.

In 1687–88 he noted that it contains "a mustard like sauce, which consisted of crayfish corrupted (fermented fish); which they called kapi." Another Westerner historical account of nam phrik comes from Jean-Baptiste Pallegoix, a French missionary who lived in Thailand in 1838.

The chef David Thompson, an acknowledged expert on Thai cuisine, writes, "They are at the very core of Thai cooking and have fed the Thai from their distant past to the present." Chili peppers originated in the Americas, where they have been cultivated for over 6,000 years.
They were probably introduced to Asia, and Thailand, in the 16th century by Portuguese emissaries and traders in what is known as the Columbian Exchange.

name: Nam phrik long ruea
sections: Shared dishes > Dipping sauces and pastes
summary: Nam phrik long ruea (Thai: น้ำพริกลงเรือ; pronounced [nám pʰrík lōŋ rɯa̯]) is a side dish in Thai cuisine, a kind of fried nam phrik (dipping sauce) that is normally eaten with vegetables.
fun_fact_candidates: It was supposedly first served in the era of King Rama V (1868–1910) on a boat trip to the Suan Snanndha palace.
story_candidates: Suan Sunanddha Palace was the first place to cook the dish.
Every royal dish that is served in the palace is said to have originated there.
Queen Sadub Ladawan is supposed to have created the recipe for an onboard picnic of two sister princesses – Sohmdet Ying Naawy (สมเด็จหญิงน้อย) and Sohmdet Ying Glaang (สมเด็จหญิงกลาง).

learn_more.title: Books about Nam phrik long ruea (Open Library)

name: Nam phrik num
sections: Shared dishes > Dipping sauces and pastes
summary: Nam Phrik Num (Thai: น้ำพริกหนุ่ม, pronounced [nám pʰrík nùm]) is a kind of “Nam phrik” of Lao origin.

name: Nam phrik phao
sections: Shared dishes > Dipping sauces and pastes
summary: Nam phrik phao (Thai: น้ำพริกเผา) is a type of Thai chili sauce known as nam phrik.

name: Nam tok (food)
summary: Nam tok (Lao: ນ້ຳຕົກ, pronounced [nâm tók]; Thai: น้ำตก, RTGS: nam tok, pronounced [nám tòk]; Northeastern Thai: น้ำตก, pronounced [nȁm tǒk]) is either a soup or a meat salad from Southeast Asia.
fun_fact_candidates: The meat salad in Lao cuisine is a sliced beef steak instead of minced meat version of larb, Laos' national dish.
One of the most popular variants of the nam tok noodle soup is known as kuai-tiao mu nam tok.
It is traditionally eaten with sticky rice and comes with raw vegetables such as thua fak yao (Thai: ถั่วฝักยาว, yardlong beans) and kalam pli (Thai: กะหล่ำปลี, cabbage).

name: Nam tok mu
summary: Nam tok mu (Thai: น้ำตกหมู, Thai pronunciation: [nám tòk mǔː]; Northeastern Thai: หมูน้ำตก, mu nam tok) is a salad of grilled and sliced pork in the Isan (northeastern Thai) and Lao culinary tradition.
story_candidates: In Laos, a closely related preparation is known as ping sin nam tok (ປີ້ງຊີ້ນນໍ້າຕົກ).
Nam tok mu is part of the broader family of grilled-meat salads that originated in Isan (northeastern Thailand) and Laos, a region whose cuisine shares strong continuities across the Mekong river.

learn_more.title: Books about Nam tok mu (Open Library)

name: Nasi kerabu
summary: Nasi kerabu (Jawi: ناسي کرابو; Kelantanese: nasik kabu) is a type of nasi ulam in essence a Malay rice dish in which rice naturally coloured with butterfly pea flowers (Clitoria ternatea) served with sides of dried fish or fried chicken, stuffed peppers (solok lada), fried crackers and other herbs and greens; all of these side dishes often times mixed akin to a salad before eaten.
fun_fact_candidates: Nasi kerabu is very popular in the east coast states of Peninsular Malaysia such as Kelantan and Terengganu, and now can be found throughout Malaysia as well as in Pattani also known by its Thai name ข้าวยำ khao yam (also anglicised as khao yum or calqued as rainbow rice salad).
story_candidates: Kerabu is one of the traditional types of salads made from vegetables and herbs in Malaysian cuisine.

In terms of its composition, nasi kerabu is similar to a number of other Malaysian national dish, in particular, nasi ulam, in which a portion of rice is also supplemented with vegetable salad and some other side dishes, and even considered as a kind of the latter.

Nasi kerabu is a traditional dish of the northeastern coast of the Malay Peninsula, primarily in the Malaysian states of Kelantan and Terengganu, from where it spread to the other regions of the country by the beginning of the 21st century, as well as to neighbouring Singapore.
This dish is also very popular in the adjacent regions of southern Thailand, populated mainly by Malays, among whom there are separatist sentiments.

Due to the latter circumstance, nasi kerabu is often perceived in this area not only as the most important culinary speciality, but also as one of the informal symbols of Malay ethnic identity and connection with similar peoples in Malaysia.

name: Nom yen
summary: Nom yen (Thai: นมเย็น, pronounced [nōm jēn]) (also known as นมชมพู) is an iced beverage from Thailand.

name: Oliang
summary: Oliang (Thai: โอเลี้ยง, pronounced [ʔōːlía̯ŋ], also spelt oleang and olieng), commonly known as Thai iced coffee, is a popular Thai beverage.

name: Pad see ew
summary: Pad see ew (phat si-io or pad siew, Thai: ผัดซีอิ๊ว, RTGS: phat si-io, pronounced [pʰàt sīːʔíw]) is a stir-fried noodle dish that is commonly eaten in Thailand.
fun_fact_candidates: It can be found easily among street food vendors and is also common in Thai restaurants around the world.

learn_more.title: Books about Pad see ew (Open Library)

name: Pandanus amaryllifolius
summary: Pandanus amaryllifolius is a tropical plant in the Pandanus (screwpine) genus, which is commonly known as pandan ( or ~ PUN-done; Malay: [ˈpandan]).
story_candidates: The leaves are used in the perfume industry and traditional medicine.

name: Pastel de nata
summary: Pastel de nata (Portuguese: [pɐʃˈtɛl dɨ ˈnatɐ]; literally, cream pastry; pl.: pastéis de nata) is a Portuguese egg custard tart pastry, optionally dusted with cinnamon.
fun_fact_candidates: Outside Portugal, they are particularly popular in other parts of Western Europe, former Portuguese colonies, such as Brazil, Mozambique, Macau, Goa, Malacca and Timor-Leste, and other parts of Asia.
In Indonesia, this pastry is especially popular in Kampung Tugu, Jakarta, a culturally Portuguese (Mardijker) enclave.
story_candidates: Pastéis de nata tarts are pastries inspired by an original recipe called pastéis de Belém, which were created before the 18th century by Catholic monks at the Jerónimos Monastery in the civil parish of Belém, in Lisbon.

In the aftermath of the Liberal Revolution of 1820, following the dissolution of religious orders and in the face of the impending closure of many convents and monasteries, the monks started selling pastéis de nata at a nearby sugar refinery to bring in revenue.
In 1834, the monastery was closed and the recipe sold to the sugar refinery, whose owners opened the Fábrica de Pastéis de Belém in 1837.
Since the opening of Fábrica de Pastéis de Belém, the original recipe that inspired pastel de nata varieties is kept in a secret room.

The Fábrica de Pastéis de Belém is, therefore, the only place in the world that produces the original pastry that inspired many variations commonly known as "pastéis de nata"; the shop is located just a short three-minute walk from the Jerónimos Monastery.
In 2009, The Guardian listed pastéis de Belém as one of the 50 "best things to eat" in the world.
In 2011, following the result of a public vote, the pastry was announced as one of Portugal's Seven Wonders of Gastronomy, further cementing it as one of the country's most popular national dishes.

learn_more.title: Books about Pastel de nata (Open Library)

name: Phallus indusiatus
summary: Phallus indusiatus, commonly called the basket stinkhorn, bamboo mushrooms, bamboo pith, long net stinkhorn, crinoline stinkhorn, bridal veil, or veiled lady, is a species of fungus in the family Phallaceae, known as stinkhorns.
fun_fact_candidates: First described scientifically in 1798 by French botanist Étienne Pierre Ventenat, the species has often been referred to a separate genus Dictyophora along with other Phallus species featuring an indusium.
It has a recorded history of use in Chinese medicine extending back to the 7th century CE and features in Nigerian folklore.
story_candidates: Phallus indusiatus has many common names based on its appearance, including long net stinkhorn, crinoline stinkhorn, basket stinkhorn, bridal veil fungus, and veiled lady.
A Chinese common name that alludes to its typical growth habitat is "bamboo mushroom" (simplified Chinese: 竹荪; traditional Chinese: 竹蓀; pinyin: zhúsūn).
Traditional medicine properties have been ascribed to Phallus indusiatus in a Chinese Tang dynasty pharmacopoeia.
Southern China's Miao people continue to use it traditionally for a number of afflictions.

It has been prescribed as Traditional Chinese Medicine as a treatment for laryngitis, leucorrhea, fever, and oliguria (low urine output), diarrhea, hypertension, cough, hyperlipidemia, and in anticancer therapy.

name: Phanaeng
summary: Phanaeng (Thai: พะแนง) also spelled Panang, is a type of Thai curry distinguished by its thick, creamy texture and mildly sweet, aromatic flavor.
fun_fact_candidates: The dish originated in central Thailand, and is typically prepared with a red curry–based paste cooked in coconut cream until the oils separate, creating a rich sauce that coats the meat.
Older preparations may also involve techniques like grilling the meat before simmering, reflecting traditional regional cooking practices.
Today, Phanaeng remains a popular Thai curry both within Thailand and internationally.
story_candidates: Early Thai cookbook Tam Raa Kap Khao (ตำรากับข้าว), printed in 1889, already mentioned kai phanaeng (ไก่พะแนง).
This dish is said to have originated in that era.
It was later prepared in the palace style before becoming a popular dish in restaurants throughout Thailand.
In the late twentieth century, phanaeng became widely known outside of Thailand due to the increasing popularity of Thai restaurants abroad.

The word phanaeng (พะแนง) is believed from the Thai adaptation of the Malay word panggang, meaning “grilled.” That suggests this dish has referred is grilled or roasted meat cooked with curry paste before evolution to the thick coconut milk curry known today.

name: Phat kaphrao
sections: Shared dishes > Fried and stir-fried dishes
summary: Pad kaphrao (Thai: ผัดกะเพรา, pronounced [pʰàt kà.pʰrāw]; transl. stir-fried holy basil), also spelled pad kaprow, pad kaprao, or pad gaprao, is one of the most popular Thai dishes in Thailand.
story_candidates: Phat kaphrao originated around the reign of King Rama VII (r. 1925–1935 CE), as Chinese immigrants in Thailand began selling it at restaurants.
Before the invention of phat kaphrao, the most similar dish was phat bai horapha (stir-fried beef and Thai basil).
Phat kraphao is considered a national dish in Thailand today but it only became popular in the country after 1957.
Phat kaphrao was included in cookbooks in the late 1970s but the method of preparation was different.
It involved marinating minced meat with liquor first, then seasoning the dish with only fish sauce and palm sugar.

name: Phat phrik khing
sections: Shared dishes > Fried and stir-fried dishes
summary: Phat phrik khing or pad prik king (Thai: ผัดพริกขิง, pronounced [pʰàt pʰrík kʰǐŋ]) is a type of Thai curry that is drier than other Thai curries such as red curry as it is fried in oil and does not contain liquid coconut milk.

learn_more.title: Books about Phat phrik khing (Open Library)

name: Pla ra
summary: Pla ra (Thai: ปลาร้า, pronounced [plāː ráː]; Northeastern Thai: ปลาแดก, pronounced [pàː dɛ̀ːk]), similar to padaek in Laos, is a traditional Thai seasoning produced by fermenting fish with rice bran or roasted rice flour and salt in a closed container for at least six months.
story_candidates: Pla ra was a common food in the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

French diplomat Simon de la Loubère, who visited Siam during the mid-Ayutthaya period (late 17th century CE), wrote about pla ra: As we eat less in Summer than in Winter, they eat less than we, by reason of the continual Summer in which they live; their common Food is Rice and Fish.
Fermented fish was popular as much as spicy Thai dip or nam phrik.

name: Pork rind
summary: Pork rind is the culinary term for the skin of a pig.

name: Pumpkin-coconut custard
summary: Pumpkin-coconut custard (Thai: สังขยาฟักทอง, sangkhaya fak thong, [sǎŋ.kʰā.jǎː fák tʰɔ̄ːŋ]; Khmer: សង់ខ្យាល្ពៅ, sangkhya lapoeu; Lao: ສັງຂະຫຍາໝາກອຶ, sangkhanya mak eu, [sǎŋ.kʰā.ɲǎ mȁːk ʔɯ́ʔ]; Northeastern Thai: สังขยาบักอึ, [sǎŋ.kʰā.ɲǎː bǎk ʔɯ̌ʔ], sangkhaya bak ue) is a Southeast Asian dessert, consisting of a coconut custard steam-baked in a whole pumpkin or kabocha.
fun_fact_candidates: It was created by Maria Guyomar de Pinha in Ayutthaya Kingdom in 17th century as an adaptation of a Portuguese egg-based dessert.
In Thailand, it is a popular dessert that is often sold in fresh food markets and as street food.

name: Punch (drink)
summary: The term punch refers to a wide assortment of drinks, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic, generally containing fruits or fruit juice.
fun_fact_candidates: The drink was introduced from the Indian subcontinent to England by employees of the East India Company in the late 17th century.
Punch is usually served at parties in large, wide bowls, known as punch bowls.
story_candidates: That etymology traces to John Fryer's A New Account of East India and Persia, in Eight Letters (1698).
Some think the word originates from the English puncheon, which was a volumetric description for certain sized barrels used to transport alcohol on ships.
From there it was introduced into other European countries.
The term punch was first recorded in English documents in 1632.
But around 1655, Jamaican-produced rum came into use, and the "modern" punch emerged.
By 1671, documents make references to punch houses.
As the need for a single-serving punch became evident, the sling, composed of spirits, water, and a sweetener, was invented.

name: Rad naa
summary: Rad naa (Thai: ราดหน้า, RTGS: radna, pronounced [râːd.nâː]; Lao: ລາດໜ້າ; literally: 'topping'), also written as rad na or lad na, is a Thai-Chinese noodle dish.

name: Red curry
summary: Red curry (Thai: แกงเผ็ด, RTGS: kaeng phet, pron. [kɛːŋ pʰèt], lit. 'spicy curry') is a Thai dish consisting of red curry paste cooked in coconut milk with meat such as chicken, beef, pork, duck or shrimp added, or else a vegetarian protein source such as tofu.

name: Roti sai mai
summary: Roti sai mai (Thai: โรตีสายไหม, pronounced [rōː.tīː.sǎːj.mǎj]; sai mai meaning 'silk thread') is a Southeast Asian dessert from Thailand.
story_candidates: The recipe was initially brought to the Ayutthaya Kingdom by Indian Muslim traders, who produced and marketed the sweet among communities.

learn_more.title: Books about Roti sai mai (Open Library)

name: Sai krok Isan
summary: Sai krok Isan (Thai: ไส้กรอกอีสาน, pronounced [sâj krɔ̀ːk ʔīː.sǎːn]; Northeastern Thai: ไส้กรอกอีสาน, ไส้อั่ว, pronounced [sàj kɔ̀ːk ʔìː.sǎn, sàj ʔúa]) is a fermented sausage originating from northeastern provinces of Thailand.
fun_fact_candidates: TasteAtlas, a global food and travel guide known for ranking traditional dishes from around the world, released its list of the Top 100 Best Sausages in the World in July 2025.
story_candidates: It is believed that the process evolved as a way to preserve food when refrigeration was not available.

Traditional preparation methods involved mixing leftover meat with glutinous rice, garlic, and salt, then stuffing the mixture into cleaned intestines and fermenting for 3–4 days until it developed a sour taste.
The technique was traditionally made during community gatherings and seasonal festivals, and the fermentation process relied on naturally occurring bacteria like Pediococcus cerevisiae.

Isan sausages are found in region's "Heet Sip Song" (12 monthly merit-making festivals, such as Bung Bang Fai) and various community celebrations throughout the year, and it symbolized the resourcefulness of Isan ancestors in food preservation.
Developed over time, the heritage of Sai krok Isan has adapted to modern ingredients and processes.
Isan sausage displays Thai traditions and culinary development while continuing to adapt to meet the modern standards of taste and safety.
Commonly served during social gatherings and celebrations, Sai krok Isan is one of the dishes that families share.
Fermentation techniques and their methods have been passed down through tradition by generations, connecting and reflecting today's society to its roots.

learn_more.title: Books about Sai krok Isan (Open Library)

name: Sai oua
summary: Sai oua, sometimes also known as Lao sausage (Lao: ໄສ້ອັ່ວ, pronounced [sȁj ʔūa], also sai ua; Thai: ไส้อั่ว, pronounced [sâj ʔùa]; Lanna: ไส้อั่ว, pronounced [sa᷇j ʔùa]; Northeastern Thai: ไส้อั่ว, pronounced [sàj ʔúa]), is a popular type of sausage made in Laos, Myanmar, and Thailand, particularly in northern Thailand and northern Laos.
fun_fact_candidates: In Shan State, Myanmar, this sausage is known as sai long phik.
In Thailand, it is also known as northern Thai sausage or Chiang Mai sausage.
Sai oua is a staple food in Thailand's northern provinces and has also become popular in the rest of the country.
story_candidates: The sausage originates from Luang Prabang, Laos.
Luang Prabang was once the royal capital and seat of power of the Kingdom of Lan Xang (1353–1707).

At the height of its power, Luang Prabang's influence stretched from the borders of Sipsongpanna (China) to Steung Treng (Cambodia), and from the Annamite Range along the border with Vietnam to the Khorat Plateau in northeastern Thailand and its sister kingdom of Lan Na.

Sai oua was listed in a collection of favorite dishes of the former Lao royal family written by Phia Sing (1898–1967), the king's personal chef and master of ceremonies, and today it is one of several popular traditional Lao dishes.

name: SangSom
summary: SangSom (Thai: แสงโสม) is a Thai distilled spirit produced since 1979.
story_candidates: SangSom was introduced in 1979 by Thai entrepreneur Niwat Thongthammachart, who aimed to produce a locally made spirit that could compete with imported brands.
The brand quickly gained popularity due to its affordable price and availability.

name: Sarim (dessert)
summary: Sarim (Thai: ซ่าหริ่ม, pronounced [sâːrìm]; or ซาหริ่ม, pronounced [sāːrìm]) is a Thai dessert.
fun_fact_candidates: The dish is mentioned in the Kap He Chom Khrueang Khao Wan poem of King Rama II (r. 1809 – 1824), though back then it was seasoned with patchouli rather than served with ice.

name: Satay
regions: Balinese, Batak, Indo, and Chinese Indonesian
summary: Satay or sate is a Southeast Asian dish consisting of small pieces of seasoned meat, seafood or vegetables skewered on sticks and grilled over charcoal.
fun_fact_candidates: Middle Eastern kebabs introduced by Muslim traders, South Asian cooking techniques brought by Tamil and Gujarati merchants, and Chinese practices such as bamboo skewering and bite-sized portions were adapted in the port cities of Java, Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula.
Satay is widely consumed across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Thailand and the southern Philippines, where it forms part of everyday meals, street food and festive occasions.

Regional adaptations reflect local ingredients and cooking traditions, incorporating elements such as sweet soy sauce, coconut milk, turmeric and spice pastes, often served with ketupat, lontong or pickled condiments.
The dish is prepared by hawkers, restaurants and home cooks alike, and has become a familiar feature of night markets and public celebrations.
It is regarded as a national dish in Indonesia and Malaysia and remains a prominent element of hawker and street-food culture in Singapore, Thailand and Brunei.
story_candidates: Muslim merchants introduced these practices to South Asia, where they were adapted into local culinary traditions.
Satay is also popular in Suriname, where it was introduced by Javanese migrants during the colonial period.
Brought by contract workers from the Dutch East Indies in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, the dish became a part of Surinamese cuisine and is commonly known as sate.
Variants include chicken, beef, and goat satay, reflecting both Javanese culinary traditions and local adaptations.

name: Sato (drink)
summary: Sato (Thai: สาโท, RTGS: satho, pronounced [sǎː.tʰōː]) is a traditional northeastern Thailand (Isan) alcoholic fermented drink that has been made for centuries from starchy glutinous or sticky rice by growers in that region.
story_candidates: This plus the availability of commercially produced sato have increased its popularity.

name: Shumai
summary: Shumai (simplified Chinese: 烧卖; traditional Chinese: 燒賣; pinyin: shāomài; Cantonese Yale: sīu-máai; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: sio-māi; Wugniu: sau1 ma6) is a type of traditional Chinese dumpling meat made of ground pork.
story_candidates: The product was initially in the form of meat and vegetables wrapped in thin sheets, and was sold weighing only the wrapper, a tradition which is still kept in Hohhot.
In 2021, "the craft of making Shaomai at Lao Suiyuan" was awarded as a non-material cultural heritage project in Hohhot.

name: Soft-shell crab
sections: Shared dishes > Fried and stir-fried dishes
summary: Soft-shell crab is a culinary term for crabs that have recently molted their old exoskeleton and are still soft.

name: Steamed curry
sections: Shared dishes > Steamed or blanched dishes
Representative dishes > Central Thai shared dishes
summary: Steamed curry is a type of Southeast Asian curry that is traditionally cooked by steaming or roasting (on an embers) in banana leaves and served with cooked rice.
story_candidates: An alternative name for the dish in Khmer is Amok (Khmer: អាម៉ុក, Khmer pronunciation: [amŏk], meaning "to steam in banana leaves"), although Cambodian monk Chuon Nath has discouraged its use in the haa mok entry of his 1967 Khmer Dictionary.

name: Sticky rice in bamboo
summary: Sticky rice in bamboo is a common Southeast Asian dish consisting of glutinous rice roasted inside specially prepared bamboo sections of different diameters and lengths.
story_candidates: In Malaysia and Indonesia, it known as lemang, which is typically eaten during Eid-ul-Fitr celebrations, where it can be eaten with rendang.
In the Philippines, this is known as binungey.

learn_more.title: Books about Sticky rice in bamboo (Open Library)

name: Suea rong hai
summary: Suea rong hai (Thai: เสือร้องไห้, pronounced [sɯ̌a rɔ́ːŋ hâːj]; Lao: ເສືອຮ້ອງໄຫ້, pronounced [sɯ̌a hɔ̂ːŋ hȁːj]; Northeastern Thai: เสือฮ้องไห้, pronounced [sɯ̌a hɔ̏ːŋ hàːj]) is a Lao and Northeastern Thai local food cooked from brisket of beef, flavored with spices, grilled rare, sliced into small pieces, and served with sticky rice and other dishes.
fun_fact_candidates: Its name is based on a local myth, which means "crying tiger".

learn_more.title: Books about Suea rong hai (Open Library)

name: Thai curry
summary: Thai curry (Thai: แกง, romanized: kaeng, pronounced [kɛ̄ːŋ]) is a dish in Thai cuisine made from curry paste, coconut milk or water, meat, seafood, vegetables or fruit, and herbs.

name: Thai fried rice
summary: Thai fried rice (Thai: ข้าวผัด, RTGS: khao phat, pronounced [kʰâ(ː)w pʰàt]) is a variety of fried rice typical of central Thai cuisine.

learn_more.title: Books about Thai fried rice (Open Library)

name: Thai salads
summary: Salads that are internationally known as Thai salads with a few exceptions fall into four main preparation methods.

name: Thai suki
summary: Thai suki, known simply as suki (Thai: สุกี้, pronounced [sū.kîː]) in Thailand, is a Thai variant of hot pot, a communal dish where diners dip meat, seafood, noodles, dumplings and vegetables into a pot of broth cooking at the table and dip them into a spicy "sukiyaki sauce" before eating.
fun_fact_candidates: In 1957, a restaurant called Coca opened its first branch in Soi Tantawan, Bangkok, offering a modified version of the Chinese hot pot under the Japanese name of Sukiyaki.
Today the MK Restaurant chain, which opened its first restaurant in 1962 on Siam Square in Bangkok, is the most popular in Thailand with around 430 restaurants across the country and 23 in Japan.
Other popular chains include Texas and Lailai.

name: Thong yip
summary: Thong yip (Thai: ทองหยิบ, pronounced [tʰɔ̄ːŋ jìp]) or pinched gold egg yolks is one of the nine auspicious traditional Thai desserts.
fun_fact_candidates: Thong yip was brought to Ayutthaya Kingdom by Maria Guyomar de Pinha who was eventually enslaved in the royal kitchens after Phetracha gained power in the Siamese revolution of 1688.
Thong yip originates from the Portuguese sweet trouxas das caldas.
story_candidates: It is believed that when thong yip is used in blessing ceremonies or as a gift to anyone, it will bring wealth and success in work; a person can turn something ordinary into gold once picked up.

name: Thong yot
summary: Thong yot (Thai: ทองหยอด, pronounced [tʰɔ̄ːŋ jɔ̀ːt]), also known as "gold egg-yolks drops", is a Thai dessert and one of the nine auspicious traditional Thai desserts.
fun_fact_candidates: Thong yot originated in Aveiro District, Portugal.
Thong yot was adapted from ovos moles de aveiro, a Portuguese dessert, by Maria Guyomar de Pinha, who was appointed as a cook in the palace in the period of King Narai of Ayutthaya.

name: Tom kha kai
summary: Tom kha kai, tom kha gai, or Thai coconut soup (Thai: ต้มข่าไก่, pronounced [tôm kʰàː kàj]; lit. 'chicken galangal soup') is a spicy and sour hot soup with coconut milk in Thai cuisine.
story_candidates: Tom kha is a Thai soup that originated around 1890 and was first recorded in a Thai recipe book.
The earliest recorded version of the soup was called tom kha pet, and it featured duck and young galangal in a coconut milk-based curry.
Over time, chicken became a more popular protein choice and the dish evolved into the version known as tom kha kai, which is made with chicken instead of duck.
In addition to chicken, shrimp is also a popular protein option and is often referred to as tom kha kung.
Tom kha shares many base ingredients with another popular Thai soup called tom yam.

learn_more.title: Books about Tom kha kai (Open Library)

name: Tom khlong
summary: Tom khlong (Thai: ต้มโคล้ง, pronounced [tôm kʰlóːŋ]) is a sour and spicy soup with smoked dried fish and various herbs.

name: Tom som
summary: Tom som (Thai: ต้มส้ม, pronounced [tôm sôm]) is a sour soup of Thai origin which usually contains seafood or chicken.
story_candidates: According to Chumpol Jangprai, the Thai word "som" has traditionally been used to describe anything that is sour.

name: Tom yum
summary: Tom yum or tom yam (UK: , US: ; Thai: ต้มยำ, RTGS: tom yam [tôm jām] ) is a family of hot and sour Thai soups.
fun_fact_candidates: Historian Giles Milton contends that the origins of tom yum can be traced back to India, where there is a variation of hot and sour shrimp soup known as sour prawn soup.
In Thailand, tom yam is available in various types, with the most popular being tom yam nam khon (creamy tom yam soup), and tom yam nam sai (clear tom yam soup).

name: Yam khai dao
summary: Yam khai dao (Thai: ยำไข่ดาว, pronounced [jām kʰàj dāːw], "fried-egg spicy salad") is a Thai dish of fried chicken or duck eggs.

learn_more.title: Books about Yam khai dao (Open Library)

name: Yam khanom chin
summary: Yam khanom chin (Thai: ยำขนมจีน, pronounced [jām kʰà.nǒm t͡ɕīːn]; also spelled Yum khanohm jeen) is a spicy and sour Thai dish made with khanom chin; thin rice noodles that and are most commonly eaten as part of the cuisines of East and Southeast Asia.

learn_more.title: Books about Yam khanom chin (Open Library)

name: Yellow curry
summary: Yellow curry, known in Thai as kaeng kari (Thai: แกงกะหรี่, lit. 'curry curry', pronounced [kɛ̄ːŋ kā.rìː]) is a Thai dish made from cumin, coriander, turmeric, fenugreek, garlic, salt, bay leaf, lemongrass, cayenne pepper, ginger, makrut lime, mace and cinnamon.

name: Yolk
summary: Among animals which produce eggs, the yolk (; also known as the vitellus) is the nutrient-bearing portion of the egg, the primary function of which is to supply food for the development of the embryo.

name: Adana kebabı
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Adana kebap (Turkish: Adana kebabı) or Adana kebab is a dish that consists of a long strip of hand-minced meat, mounted on a wide iron skewer and grilled on an open mangal filled with burning charcoal.
fun_fact_candidates: The kebab is named after Adana, the fifth-largest city of Turkey, and was originally known as the kıyma kebabı (lit: minced meat kebab) or kıyma in Adana-Mersin and the southeastern provinces of Turkey.
story_candidates: The version prepared and consumed today in the province of Adana also has a history rooted in the modern Turkish culture, only to receive a "Controlled Designation of Origin" in February 2005, after several legal trials.

name: Alinazik kebab
summary: Alinazik kebab, or simply Ali Nazik, is a home-style Turkish dish which is a specialty of the Gaziantep province of Turkey.

name: Allspice
summary: Allspice, also known as Jamaica pepper, myrtle pepper, pimenta, or pimento, is the dried unripe berry of Pimenta dioica, a midcanopy tree native to the Greater Antilles, southern Mexico (in Nahuatl: xocoxochitl), and Central America, now cultivated in many warm parts of the world.
fun_fact_candidates: The name allspice was coined as early as 1621 by the English, who valued it as a spice that combined the flavours of cinnamon, nutmeg, and clove.

name: Analı kızlı soup
summary: Analı kızlı soup is a soup from Turkey (Adana, Tarsus, Gaziantep, Kahramanmaraş, Malatya) which includes meatballs, tomato, bulgur, and chickpeas. 'Analı kızlı' means, literally, 'with daughters and mothers', daughters being the chickpeas, and mothers the bulgur balls (i.e., meatballs covered with a thin layer of bulgur), all in a soup like a yogurt sauce.
fun_fact_candidates: It is a part of traditional Turkish cuisine.

learn_more.title: Books about Analı kızlı soup (Open Library)

name: Arnavut ciğeri
summary: Arnavut ciğeri (literally "Albanian liver") is a Turkish dish made of oil-fried lamb or veal liver cubes seasoned with hot pepper, served traditionally with onion and parsley.
story_candidates: The word Arnavut (Albanian) is part of a dish in Istanbul cuisine known as Arnavut ciğeri (Albanian liver).

In the late 17th century, Albanians were noted by Ottoman traveler Evliya Çelebi as being butchers in Istanbul originating from Ohrid, Korçë and Hurupişte (modern Argos Orestiko) selling lamb meat cuts like liver, heart and kidneys.

The dish Arnavut ciğeri became part of Turkish cuisine during the Ottoman period, when Ottomans assimilated culinary traditions from peoples they encountered and merged them with their own cuisine, cooking practices and customs.

name: Aush reshteh
sections: Typical food and drinks > Main course > Soup and āsh
summary: Aush reshteh or ash-e-reshteh (Persian: آش رشته) is a type of āsh (Iranian thick soup) featuring reshteh (thin noodles), kidney beans, chickpeas, lentils, herbs, and kashk (a sour dairy product made from cooked or dried yogurt), commonly made in Iran.
story_candidates: Traditionally, aush reshteh is served at special Iranian events like Nowruz or Sizdah Be-dar, or during wintertime.
The noodles are supposed to symbolize good fortune for the new year.

name: Açma
summary: Açma is a slightly sweet yeast pastry from Turkish cuisine that is often offered as street food.
story_candidates: Açma is popular and widespread throughout Turkey.

name: Barbunya pilaki
summary: Barbunya pilaki is a traditional Turkish dish made with borlotti beans (known as barbunya in Turkish) stewed in olive oil with a medley of vegetables, garlic, tomato, and seasonings.
story_candidates: The word barbunya refers specifically to borlotti beans, also known as cranberry beans, which are recognized for their mottled red-pink skins before cooking.

name: Bazlama
summary: Bazlama is a leavened, circular flatbread from Turkish cuisine with a soft, fluffy texture and slightly crisp exterior.
fun_fact_candidates: After baking, it is generally consumed fresh and is often served as part of a traditional Turkish breakfast.
Bazlama is sometimes referred to as "village bread" due to its popularity in rural areas of Turkey.

name: Beyaz peynir
sections: Dishes and foods > Dairy products > Cheeses
summary: Beyaz peynir (Turkish pronunciation: [beˈjaz pejniɾ], 'white cheese') is a brine cheese produced from unpasteurized sheep, cow or goat milk.
fun_fact_candidates: It is eaten plain, for example as part of the traditional Turkish breakfast, used in salads, and incorporated into cooked foods such as menemen, börek, gözleme, and pide.

name: Beyti kebab
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Beyti is a Turkish dish consisting of ground beef or lamb, grilled on a skewer and served wrapped in lavash and topped with tomato sauce and yogurt.
fun_fact_candidates: The dish is named after Beyti Güler, the owner of the popular restaurant Beyti in Istanbul.
He was inspired to create his own dish in 1961, after witnessing Swiss butcher Möller's method of preparing meat, when he was visiting Switzerland.

name: Bici bici
summary: Bici bici or bicibici muhallebisi is a Turkish dessert.

name: Boortsog
summary: Boortsog, boorsoq, baursak, baursaq, bauyrsaq, borsok, or boorsok is a fried dough food found in the cuisines of Central Asia, Idel-Ural, Mongolia, and the Middle East.

name: Borani
summary: Borani (Persian: بورانی, romanized: bowrâni) is a salad dish from Iranian cuisine.
fun_fact_candidates: Borani is also popular in the Caucasus and Afghanistan.

name: Buğu kebabı
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Buğu kebabı (Turkish for vapour kebab) is a lamb-based dish from the Turkish cuisine.

name: Cardamom
summary: Cardamom (), sometimes cardamon or cardamum, is a spice made from the seeds of several plants in the genera Elettaria and Amomum in the family Zingiberaceae.
fun_fact_candidates: The first references to cardamom are found in Sumer, and in Ayurveda.
In the 21st century, it is cultivated mainly in India, Indonesia, and Guatemala.
story_candidates: In China, Amomum was an important part of the economy during the Song Dynasty (960–1279).
In 1150, the Arab geographer Muhammad al-Idrisi noted that cardamom was being imported to Aden, in Yemen, from India and China.
The Portuguese became involved in the trade in the 16th century, and the industry gained wide-scale European interest in the 19th century.

name: Cağ kebabı
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Cağ kebabı (Turkish: [ˈdʒaː ceˈbabɯ]) is a horizontally stacked marinated rotating lamb kebab variety, originating in Erzurum Province, Turkey.
fun_fact_candidates: Cağ kebabı was registered and granted a geographical indication as 'Erzurum Oltu Cağ Kebabı' by the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office in 2010.
Note that while it is increasingly available in most Turkish cities, the Cağ kebabı is especially popular in Erzurum, whereas enjoying an ever-growing success in Istanbul and Ankara.
story_candidates: Ottoman travel books of the eighteenth century cite a kebab cooked on wood fire consisting of a horizontal stack of meat, known as "Cağ Kebabı" in the Eastern Turkish province of Erzurum.
Now, the kebab is very famous in Erzurum, Istanbul and many states in the EU.

name: Chorba
summary: Chorba, ( CHOR-bə; Turkish: [tʃɔɾˈba]) shorwa, shurba, shurpa, shurbah or shorba ( SHOR-bə) is a broad class of stews or rich soups found in national cuisines across North Africa, the Middle East, Iran, Turkey, Central and Eastern Europe, Central Asia, East Africa and South Asia.

name: Circassian cheese
sections: Dishes and foods > Dairy products > Cheeses
summary: Circassian cheese (Adyghe: адыгэ къуае Adyghe pronunciation: [aːdəɣa qʷaːja], Russian: адыгейский сыр adygeyskiy syr), is a cheese found across the North Caucasus, the Levant and other areas with a Circassian diaspora.
fun_fact_candidates: There is an annual festival for Circassian cheese in Maykop, the capital of the Republic of Adyghea, Russia, held during the Circassian cultural festival with participants from different regions in the North Caucasus, competing in producing the best types of Circassian cheese.
The small Circassian community in Israel, most of whom live in Kfar Kama and Rehaniya in the Upper Galilee, operates boutique dairies that produce traditional Circassian cheese.

name: Circassian chicken
summary: Circassian chicken (Adyghe: Адыгэ чэты; Kabardian: Адыгэ джэд) is a dish of shredded boiled chicken served under or in a rich paste made with crushed walnuts, and stock thickened with stale bread.
fun_fact_candidates: Although it was typically served as a main course, it became popular as an appetizer.
A similar walnut sauce and a chicken dish made with this sauce is known as satsivi in Georgian cuisine.

name: Ciğer kebabı
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Ciğer kebabı (English: liver kebab) is a common type of skewered meat served in Anatolian cuisine, usually eaten with sliced onions, salad and bread.

name: Cornbread
summary: Cornbread is a quick bread made with cornmeal, popular in the cuisine of the Southern United States, with origins in Native American cuisine.
story_candidates: First domesticated in Mexico around six thousand years ago, corn was introduced to what is now the United States between three thousand and one thousand years ago.
Native cooks developed a number of recipes based on corn, including cornbread, that were later adopted by European settlers and slaves —especially those who lived in Southern colonies.

Although Native people in the Americas first cultivated corn, it was introduced in West Africa by European traders shortly after contact through the Atlantic slave trade, and quickly became a major staple in African cooking.

name: Crushed red pepper
summary: Crushed red pepper or red pepper flakes or chilli flakes is a condiment or spice consisting of dried and crushed (as opposed to ground) red chilli peppers.
fun_fact_candidates: Often there is a high ratio of seeds, which are often erroneously believed to contain the most heat.
Crushed red chilli pepper in Turkey, served as a common condiment with very few seeds, is known as pul biber.
story_candidates: Red chilli peppers, which are a part of the Solanaceae (nightshade) family, were first found in Central and South America and have been harvested for use since about 7,500 BCE.
Spanish explorers were introduced to the pepper while on a search for black pepper.
Southern Italians popularized crushed red chilli peppers in the 19th century and heavily used them in the U.S. when they migrated there.

learn_more.title: Books about Crushed red pepper (Open Library)

name: Dondurma
summary: Dondurma is the Turkish name for ice cream, while Booza (Arabic: بُوظَة, romanized: Būẓah, lit. 'ice cream') is the Arabic name for ice cream.
fun_fact_candidates: Outside of the Middle East, it typically refers specifically to mastic ice cream, which is often believed to originate from the city and region of Kahramanmaraş and is known as maraş dondurma in Turkish.
story_candidates: Food historian Priscilla Mary Işın wrote in Ottoman Culinary Dictionary that it is unknown when salep-based milk dondurma was first made, though she notes that the earliest recipe dates back to 1882.
The 1882 recipe appeared in a cookbook titled Ev Kadını credited to Ayse Fahriye.
Mary Işın also notes the diverging traditions of making ice cream: Italian recipes of the time used eggs to thicken ice cream where as the Turkish recipe used salep.

name: Doner kebab
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Doner kebab or döner kebab is a Turkish dish made of meat cooked on a vertical rotisserie.
fun_fact_candidates: The vertical rotisserie was invented in the 19th-century Ottoman Empire, and dishes such as the Arab shawarma, Greek gyros, Greek-Canadian donair, and Mexican al pastor are derived from the rotisserie technique of this dish.
The modern sandwich variant of doner kebab originated and was popularized in 1970s West Berlin by Turkish immigrants.
This was recognised by the Berlin-based Association of Turkish Döner Manufacturers in Europe in 2011.

The sliced meat of a doner kebab may be served on a plate with various accompaniments, stuffed into a pita or other type of bread as a sandwich, or wrapped in a thin flatbread such as lavash or filo, known as a dürüm (literally meaning roll or wrap in Turkish).
Kadir Nurman in the early 1970s introduced the sandwich or wrap form, which has become popular around the world as a fast food dish sold by kebab shops, and is often called simply a "kebab".
story_candidates: In the Ottoman Empire, at least as far back as the 17th century, stacks of seasoned sliced meat were cooked on a horizontal rotisserie, similar to the cağ kebab.
The vertical rotisserie was introduced no later than the mid-19th century.
According to Yavuz İskenderoğlu, his grandfather İskender Efendi as a child in 1850s Bursa had the idea of roasting the lamb at his father's restaurant vertically rather than horizontally.
It was a success, and some years later became known as doner kebap.
However, he may have been preceded by Hamdi Usta from Kastamonu around 1830.
A version popular in the Arab world became known as shawarma.
By at least the 1930s, it had been brought overseas, and was sold in restaurants in Mexico by Lebanese immigrants.
The Greek variation was likely brought to Greece proper by Greek refugees in the 1920s, due to the population exchange between Greece and Turkey, later transforming into gyros.
It was not until a century after its invention that doner kebab was introduced and popularized in Istanbul, most famously by Beyti Güler.
His restaurant, first opened in 1945, was soon discovered by journalists and began serving doner and other kebab dishes to kings, prime ministers, film stars and celebrities.

name: Durum wheat
sections: Dishes and foods > Pilav and pasta
summary: Durum (), also called pasta wheat or macaroni wheat (Triticum durum or Triticum turgidum subsp. durum), is a tetraploid species of wheat.

name: Düğün çorbası
summary: Düğün çorbası (Turkish: Düğün çorbası) is the Turkish cuisine soup on lamb or beef broth.
fun_fact_candidates: Now is a popular dish for every day, mainly in the cold season, but initially the hearty soup Düğün çorbası was the opening meal on a wedding feast in the village, which could continue according to tradition for forty days and forty nights.

name: Eggplant kebab
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Eggplant kebab (Turkish: Patlıcan kebap /pɑːˈdɯˈɪŋʒɑːn keˈbaːp/, Gaziantep dialect of Turkish: balcan kebabı, Arabic: كباب باذنجان) is a Turkish kebab (meat dish) that may be prepared according to various traditions.
fun_fact_candidates: In the area of Şanlıurfa Birecik and other parts of Southern Turkey, people traditionally would prepare a tray of eggplant kebab from leftover eggplant and chicken meat at home, then take it to a local bakery to be cooked in the wood-fired oven.

name: Ezogelin soup
summary: Ezogelin soup or Ezo gelin soup (Turkish: Ezogelin çorbası, "the soup of Ezo the bride") is a common soup in Turkish cuisine.

name: Fava (Turkish dish)
summary: Fava, also known as bakla ezmesi, is a traditional Turkish dish made of dried fava beans (broad beans, called bakla in Turkish), which are soaked and dehulled, leaving the deeper green split inner seeds.
fun_fact_candidates: Fava originated in Byzantine cuisine; it was widely served in tavernes.

name: Fish soup
summary: Fish soup is a food made by combining fish or seafood with vegetables and stock, juice, water, or another liquid.
fun_fact_candidates: Traditionally, soups are classified into two main groups: clear soups and thick soups.
Other ingredients commonly used to thicken soups and broths include rice, lentils, flour, and grains; many popular soups also include carrots and potatoes.
Bisques are heavy cream soups traditionally prepared with shellfish, but can be made with any type of seafood or puree of vegetables or fruits.

name: Gilt-head bream
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Fish
summary: The gilt-head bream (Sparus aurata), also known as the gilthead, dourade, gilt-head seabream, European seabream or silver seabream, is a species of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the family Sparidae, the seabreams or porgies.
story_candidates: Gilt-head seabream have traditionally been cultured extensively in coastal lagoons and saltwater ponds.
However, intensive rearing systems were developed during the 1980s, and gilt-head seabream has become an important aquaculture species, primarily in the Mediterranean area and Portugal.
Reported production was negligible until the late 1980s, but reached 140,000 metric tons (140,000 long tons; 150,000 short tons) in 2010, thus dwarfing the capture fisheries production.

name: Glasswort salad
summary: Glasswort salad or samphire salad (Turkish: Deniz börülcesi salatası) is a salad in Turkish cuisine.

name: Gözleme
summary: Gözleme is a savory Turkish stuffed turnover.
story_candidates: The oldest record of the word in a Turkic language is dated back to 1477.
It is first attested in Persian-Turkish dictionary Lügat-i Halîmî and also found in Evliya Çelebi's Seyahatnâme.

name: Haydari
summary: Haydari is a type of yogurt dish similar to a thick cacık, made from certain herbs and spices, combined with garlic and yogurt.

name: Hünkârbeğendi
summary: Hünkârbeğendi, or simply beğendi (literally, 'the sovereign is pleased'), is an eggplant and meat (lamb or beef) dish in Ottoman cuisine.

name: İskender kebap
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: İskender kebap is a Turkish dish that consists of sliced meat topped with hot tomato sauce over pieces of pita bread, and generously slathered with melted special sheep's milk butter and yogurt.
fun_fact_candidates: It is one of the most popular dishes of Turkey.

It takes its name from its inventor, İskender, who lived in Bursa in the late 19th century Ottoman Empire. "Kebapçı İskender" is trademarked by the İskenderoğlu family, who still run the restaurant in Bursa.

name: İskilip dolması
summary: Iskilip dolması is a Turkish dish of caramelized onions, rice and lamb that was traditionally cooked in a cloth bag in a large copper pot or cauldron.
fun_fact_candidates: The dish is a regional specialty of Çorum, where it is prepared in large quantities using traditional methods and is typically served at weddings.
First the meat is added to the pot with some water.
The meat broth is used to prepare a noodle soup that is traditionally served as an appetizer and flour helva made with milk is prepared as a dessert.
Some modern cooks have adapted the recipe for preparation in home kitchens.
Onions are first sautéd in a large amount of butter until caramelized.

name: Kalehjoosh
sections: Typical food and drinks > Main course > Soup and āsh
summary: Kalehjoosh (Persian: کاله‌جوش), or Kyalagyosh (Armenian: քյալագյոշ) is a popular traditional soup in Iran, Armenia, Azerbaijan (Azerbaijani: Kələcoş), and Turkey (Turkish: Keledoş, Kelecoş, or Kelecaşı).
fun_fact_candidates: It is believed to be of Armenian origin due to Its etymology.

name: Karnıyarık
summary: Karnıyarık (lit. 'riven belly') is a Turkish dish of eggplant stuffed with a mix of sautéed chopped onions, garlic, black pepper, tomatoes, optional green pepper, parsley, and ground meat.
fun_fact_candidates: The eggplant is traditionally fried, though it can also be roasted.

name: Kars gravyer cheese
sections: Dishes and foods > Dairy products > Cheeses
summary: Kars gravyer is a Turkish cheese similar to Emmental although its name suggests Gruyère.
fun_fact_candidates: Kars gravyer originated in 1878 when David Moser, a Swiss cheese producer, stopped in Boğatepe, and found the region suitable for cheese making.

learn_more.title: Books about Kars gravyer cheese (Open Library)

name: Kavurma
summary: Kavurma is a broad type of fried or sautéed meat dish found in Turkish cuisine.
story_candidates: In Central Asia the dish is known as Kuurdak.

name: Kağıt kebabı
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Kağıt kebabı is a type of Turkish kebab peculiar to Hatay province and its administrative capital Antakya.

name: Kesme
sections: Dishes and foods > Pilav and pasta
summary: Kesme or erişte is a type of egg noodle found in various Central Asian countries.
fun_fact_candidates: Kesme is traditionally a homemade dish, and not often found at restaurants or cafés.
In Turkey, kesme is also known as "erişte", and eaten generally in winter.

name: Keşkek
sections: Dishes and foods > Pilav and pasta
summary: Keşkek, also known as kashkak, kashkek, or keške, is a ceremonial meat or chicken and wheat or barley stew found in Turkish, Iranian, Greek, Armenian, and Balkan cuisines.
fun_fact_candidates: In 2011, keşkek was confirmed to be an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Turkey by UNESCO.
story_candidates: The first known written reference to the dish is found in a copy of Danishmendname dating back to 1360.

Keşkek is documented in Iran and the region of Syria by Turkish tribes as early as the 15th century; it is still consumed by many today, traditionally during religious festivals, weddings and funerals.
Under the name of κεσκέκ, κεσκέκι and κισκέκ (keskék, keskéki, and kiskék), it is a festival dish in Lesbos and among Pontian Greeks.
Harissa bears strong similarities to keşkek in terms of its preparation and cooking process; however, harissa is associated with different symbolic meanings.

name: Kumpir
summary: Kumpir (also compire) is a baked potato with various fillings.
fun_fact_candidates: It is a popular fast food in the Balkans.
story_candidates: The word comes from the Palatine/Alemannic Grumbier or Grummbeere 'potato', introduced to Southeastern Europe by the Danube Swabians.
In English it is known as Turkish baked potato or compire; in French it is known as compiré.
In Western languages, particularly English and French, the traditional Turkish baked potato dish is referred to as kumpir or, in some contexts, compire or (grundbirne)..

name: Kuru fasulye
summary: Kuru fasulye is a stewed bean dish in Turkish cuisine.
fun_fact_candidates: It is often considered the national dish of Turkey.
Also known as Mash Shorbasi in Azerbaijan.

name: Kısır
summary: Kısır is a bulgur based salad found in Turkish cuisine.

name: Lavash
summary: Lavash is a thin flatbread made of leavened or unleavened wheat dough, baked in a tandoor (a type of clay oven) or on a saj griddle.
fun_fact_candidates: Lavash originated in ancient times, with several countries claiming its origin.
In the modern day, lavash is widespread in many parts of Asia between Turkey and Kashmir, and also exists in other regions where it was introduced by Armenian immigrants.
The UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List inscribed lavash "as an expression of culture in Armenia" in 2014.

This was controversial in other countries in the region, and a separate listing regarding the culture of lavash and other flatbreads in Iran, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Turkey was inscribed in 2016.
story_candidates: Sevan Nişanyan connects the Persian word for lavash to the Aramaic לושׁ lwš root meaning 'to knead' and recorded al-Faraj ba'd ash-Shiddah from 1451 as the oldest text to use the term in Turkish.
Food historian Gil Marks states that lavash originated in the Middle East and traces it to the early innovation of cooking thin flatbreads on terracotta griddles rather than directly on embers.
Claims of lavash as a uniquely Iranian tradition have existed as far back as the Arsacid dynasty of ancient Persia.

One story tells that King Arame of Urartu was captured by Assyrian forces, who would free him if he won an archery competition after ten days without food, but his messenger secretly brought him lavash hidden in his armor, enabling him to win.
In Armenian weddings, it is traditional for a lavash to be placed on the couple's shoulders as a symbol of luck, wealth, and fertility.

Many artworks depict the preparation of it, such as a painting by the Armenian American artist Manuel Tolegian, titled Armenian Ladies Baking Lavash, which was selected by U.S. President Gerald Ford to hang in the White House in 1976.

name: Macun
summary: Macun (in Turkish also Macun şekeri) is a soft, sweet and colorful Turkish toffee paste.
fun_fact_candidates: It is a street food that may be prepared with many herbs and spices.
Macun originated from spicy preparations of Mesir macunu, a traditional Turkish herbal paste from the Ottoman empire.
story_candidates: Macun originated from spicy preparations of Mesir macunu, a traditional herbal paste from the Ottoman empire.
During the Ottoman period, macun named Neruz macunu, also referred to as nevruziyye, was consumed as both a medicine and confectionery.
During the 17th century in Turkey, the dervish Seyyid Hasan denoted the consumption of two flavors of macun, respectively flavored with mint and sweet flag.
Street vendors would purvey macun to people at the Hıdırellez spring festival, on market days, holidays, at wedding processions, and at other times.

name: Mahleb
summary: Mahleb or mahlepi is an aromatic spice made from the seeds of a species of cherry, Prunus mahaleb (the Mahaleb or St Lucie cherry).

name: Meat on the bone
summary: Meat on the bone or bone-in meat is meat that is sold with some or all of the bones included in the cut or portion, i.e. meat that has not been filleted.
fun_fact_candidates: Meat on the bone is used in many traditional recipes.

learn_more.title: Books about Meat on the bone (Open Library)

name: Mihaliç peyniri
sections: Dishes and foods > Dairy products > Cheeses
summary: Mihaliç peyniri is an aged sheep's milk cheese from Turkey.

name: Pilaf
sections: Dishes and foods > Pilav and pasta
summary: Pilaf (US: or pilau UK: ) is a rice dish, or in some regions, a wheat dish, whose recipe usually involves cooking in stock or broth, adding spices, and other ingredients such as vegetables and meat, and employing some technique for achieving cooked grains that do not adhere.
fun_fact_candidates: During the Abbasid Caliphate, such methods of cooking rice first spread across a vast territory from South Asia to Spain, and eventually to a wider world.
story_candidates: It was at the time of the Abbasid Caliphate that methods of cooking rice which approximate modern styles of cooking pilaf at first spread through a vast territory from Spain to Afghanistan, and eventually to a wider world.
Kitab al-Wusla, an early 13th–century cookbook authored by Ibn al-Adim of Aleppo, provides the first recipe for a dish resembling modern pilaf, utilizing a base of rice, meat, chickpeas, and garlic.

Similarly, Alexander the Great and his army, many centuries earlier, in the 4th century BCE, have been reported to have been so impressed with the Eastern Iranic Bactrian and Sogdian palāvs that his soldiers brought the recipes back to Macedon when they returned.

name: Pilaki
summary: Pilaki is a style of meze and may refer to several dishes that are cooked in a sauce made out of onion, garlic, carrot, potato, tomato or tomato paste, sugar, and olive oil.
story_candidates: It originated in the Byzantine Empire, being used in Byzantine cuisine.

name: Piyaz
summary: Piyaz (Turkish: piyaz, Persian: پیاز, Kurdish: pivaz, piyaz for "onion" or salad) is a bean salad or meze in Turkish cuisine and Persian cuisine that is made from any kind of boiled beans with raw onion, parsley and sumac.
fun_fact_candidates: In Antalya province of Turkey it is prepared differently from other regions with other ingredients such as tarator sauce based on tahini (crushed sesame seeds).
Mung beans piyaz (maş piyazı) is famous in Gaziantep and, like Antalya piyaz, is registered with the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office.
During the Ottoman period, piyaz was also made from artichoke, pea, chickpea, broad bean and potato, which were introduced to Turkey in the last quarter of the 19th century.

name: Pogača
summary: Pogača (Cyrillic: погача; Turkish: poğaça; Hungarian: pogácsa) is a type of bread baked in the ashes of the fireplace, and later in modern ovens.

name: Poppy seed
summary: Poppy seeds are a type of oilseed obtained from the poppy plant (Papaver somniferum).
story_candidates: For instance, the Egyptian Ebers Papyrus, written c. 1550 BCE, lists the poppy seed as a sedative.

The Minoan civilization (approximately 2700 to 1450 BCE), a Bronze Age civilization which arose on the island of Crete, cultivated poppies for their seeds, and used a mixture of milk, opium and honey to calm crying babies.

name: Red mullet
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Fish
summary: The red mullets or surmullets are two species of goatfish, Mullus barbatus and Mullus surmuletus, found in the Mediterranean Sea, east North Atlantic Ocean, and the Black Sea.

name: Rose water
sections: Common dishes > Condiments, sauces and spices
summary: Rose water or rosewater is a flavoured water created by steeping rose petals in water.
fun_fact_candidates: Rose water is widely used to flavour culinary dishes and enhance cosmetic products, and it is significant in religious rituals throughout Eurasia.
Central Iran is home to the annual Golabgiri festival each spring.
Thousands of tourists visit the area to celebrate the rose harvest for the production of rosewater.
story_candidates: Rose water likely originated in Persia, where it is known as golāb (گلاب), from gul (گل rose) and ab (آب water).

name: Sheep's sorrel soup
summary: Sheep's sorrel soup (Turkish: kuzukulağı çorbası) is a soup made from sheep's sorrel leaves, water, corn, beans, onions, butter, and salt.

learn_more.title: Books about Sheep's sorrel soup (Open Library)

name: Shish kebab
sections: Dishes and foods > Meat dishes > Kebabs
summary: Shish kebab or shish kebap is a popular dish of skewered and grilled cubes of meat, originating in the Middle East.
fun_fact_candidates: It is one of the many types of kebab, a range of meat dishes originating in the Middle East.
It is traditionally made of lamb but there are also versions with various kinds of meat, poultry, or fish.
story_candidates: The word kebab alone was already present in English by the late 17th century, from the Arabic: كَبَاب (kabāb), partly via Urdu, Persian and Turkish.
According to the Oxford English Dictionary, its earliest known publication in English is in the 1914 novel Our Mr. Wrenn by Sinclair Lewis.

name: Stuffed mussels
summary: Stuffed mussels (Turkish: Midye dolma; Armenian: Լցոնած միդիա, or Միդիա տոլմա), or midye, is a generic name for plump orange mussels that contain herbed and spiced rice.
fun_fact_candidates: Midye dolma is a popular and common street food snack in the coastal cities of Turkey and in Armenia.
story_candidates: Maggakis' 1888 work Bizans Salnamesi Armenians had used big mussels and prepared the dish using sheep's tail fat or "zibir yağı", a solid fat imported from Siberia.
Balıkhane Nazırı Ali Rıza Bey (1842–1928) also notes that in Bahariye, Kadıköy brickworks owner Şahbaz Efendi's Armenian cook was preparing stuffed mussels.
During the 19th century it was reported that İstanbulite Turkish women were also cooking stuffed mussels.
In the 1960s, the preparation and sale of stuffed mussels came to be dominated by immigrants from Mardin, who had at the time recently immigrated to İstanbul's Galata district.
